title: Investigating Digital Self-Tracking for Monitoring Physical Activity in CVD Patients
author: Jürgen ogel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jhacj2e

steps.title: Define eligibility criteria
steps.instruction: Specify inclusion criteria (male out‑patients, age 40‑80, CVD diagnosis (STEMI, NSTEMI, PCI or revascularisation) within 3 months, clinically stable ≥2 weeks, able to join rehab, consent, personal computer with Internet) and exclusion criteria (Parkinson’s disease, uncontrolled atrial/ventricular dysrhythmias, inability to perform MVPA or complete rehab for medical reasons).

steps.title: Recruit and obtain consent
steps.instruction: Select eligible male patients attending outpatient cardiac rehabilitation phase II, explain the study, obtain written informed consent, and record baseline demographic data.

steps.title: Randomise participants
steps.instruction: Use a standard software‑based random sample generator to assign participants 1:1 to the study group (activity tracker) or control group (no tracker).

steps.title: Introductory information session
steps.instruction: Conduct a face‑to‑face conversation of ≈30 minutes covering purpose, procedures, benefits/risks, medication and lifestyle effects, possible symptoms, side‑effects, premature termination, data use, costs, reimbursement, remuneration, and contact details; provide the same information in written, easy‑to‑understand form.

steps.title: Enroll in routine cardiac rehabilitation
steps.instruction: Enroll all participants in the standard cardiac rehabilitation programme for the first six weeks, including heart‑rate‑controlled moderate‑to‑vigorous physical activity, nutritional education, and psychological support; exercises are partly supervised at the centre and partly at home; keep all medication regimens unchanged.

steps.title: Baseline graded exercise test
steps.instruction: At week 1 (t1) perform a graded exercise test on an electronically braked cycle ergometer or treadmill using an individual ramp protocol (8‑12 min to peak) per national/international guidelines; monitor heart rate continuously with a conventional 12‑lead ECG (10 electrodes) and measure blood pressure manually; start with unloaded pedalling warm‑up, increase work rate regularly, and continue until exhaustion or ECG termination criteria are met, recording maximum power (W).

steps.title: Distribute activity trackers
steps.instruction: On the day of t1 give each study‑group participant a consumer‑grade wrist‑worn 3‑D accelerometer (bracelet‑shaped) with ≥7 day storage, customize the bracelet size to the wrist, and provide a user manual.

steps.title: Instruct device use and data sync
steps.instruction: Tell participants to wear the tracker on the non‑dominant wrist 24 h/day, 7 days/week; charge the rechargeable battery via USB or charging unit; install the synchronising software on their PC/laptop using the supplied installation guide with screenshots; synchronise data at least once per week to overcome limited storage; set the web‑service privacy to the most private level and give each participant personal login data after consent.

substeps.instruction: Customize bracelet size and give user manual.
Explain display views, features, memory, charging, operating time, communication specs, and system requirements.
Assist with software download, installation, and account creation; update tracker firmware.
Set privacy preferences to maximum privacy and provide login credentials.

steps.title: Optional coaching account connection
steps.instruction: If possible, link participant accounts to a special coaching account held by the study authors; inform participants that only authors and medical staff can view their activity data and that personal identifiers will be anonymised to a study reference number.

steps.title: Provide activity‑awareness guidance
steps.instruction: Advise participants to raise awareness of their own activity, set realistic personal goals (e.g., daily step count, reduce sitting time, be more active than the previous day).

steps.title: Monitor data synchronization
steps.instruction: Check every three days whether each study‑group participant has synchronised data; if data are missing for >5 days, contact the participant by phone or e‑mail, remind them to sync, and troubleshoot any device or software issues.

steps.title: Midterm graded exercise test
steps.instruction: At week 6 (t2) repeat the graded exercise test exactly as performed at baseline, using the same ramp protocol, ECG monitoring, and blood‑pressure measurement.

steps.title: Continue interventions post‑midterm
steps.instruction: After t2, provide medical lifestyle recommendations to all participants; for weeks 7‑12 the study group continues wearing the activity tracker, while the control group receives no further intervention.

steps.title: Final graded exercise test
steps.instruction: At week 13 (t3) repeat the graded exercise test with identical protocol and measurements as at t1 and t2.

steps.title: Collect activity trackers
steps.instruction: On the day of t3 retrieve the activity trackers from all study‑group participants.

steps.title: Analyze performance and activity data
steps.instruction: Calculate each participant’s maximum power (W) and relative performance (% of individual target) from the three exercise tests; compare these values across t1, t2, and t3 and between study and control groups; analyse the synchronised activity‑tracker data for total steps, active minutes, and sedentary time.
